s: Was schlägst du vor? — Tja, ich schlage vor, dass wir ins Kino gehen.
What do you suggest? — Well, I suggest that we go to the movies.
Used to express acceptance of one's misfortune; oh well, welp
Oh well! That didn’t work out as planned...
Used as an unsympathetic response to someone else's misfortune, implying it was predictable or is otherwise simply to be accepted; tough luck
Tja, wenn er will, dass ich mich darum kümmere, dann hätte er sich rechtzeitig bei mir melden müssen.
Tough luck, if he wants me to take care of it, he should have reached out to me in good time.
Tja, dann hat sie eben Pech gehabt.
Bad luck for her, then, she's just going to need to deal with that.
tja.et: Probably from an onomatopoeia for clicking one’s tongue, which is used with the same meaning. Perhaps also a variant of ja (“yes”). Similar expressions are found in nearby Germanic languages and in Finnish, suggesting an areal feature.

Tjost.et: Inherited by the late 12th century (Hartmann von Aue) from Middle High German tjost f, tjoste f, jiust f, jiuste f, joste f, schust f, but also (more rarely) as tust m, just m, just m, gust m, tschuscht m. From Old French jouster. Cognate with English joust.

t: Tja, du hast die nun mal gewählt.
Well, now, who would have thought it?
Well, that's how it is, unfortunately.
l: Tja, in Schutt und Asche weggebombt wird dieser SPD-Haufen dann trotzdem.
Tja Kramer, das haben Deine Gesinnungsgenossen äußerst dilettantisch aufgezogen und organisiert.
Tja, wenn man es eilig hat, dann interessieren Mittelwerte einen Dreck.
